items.note: The --opacity-muted custom property (0.6) is deleted from the token scale. No component has read it since 0.10.0 moved the disabled states onto --text-disabled + --opacity-disabled, so REMOVING IT CHANGES NOTHING THE LIBRARY RENDERS. Two consumer cases. (1) You SET it - most likely on ds-button or ds-icon-button, the override 0.10.0's DELETE-LIST already warned about: delete the declaration, it was a no-op then and is a no-op now (those two resolve their disabled state from oklch(from accent ...) colours, and --ds-button-label-color-disabled / --ds-icon-button-icon-color-disabled are the real hooks). (2) You READ it in your own CSS, i.e. var(--opacity-muted) appears in a value you wrote: that now resolves to nothing and the declaration is dropped, so pick the token that names the job instead - --opacity-disabled (0.5) where opacity is the ONLY disabled signal, --opacity-text-disabled (0.38) for disabled text - or inline 0.6 if what you actually wanted was de-emphasis rather than a disabled state. Do not re-declare --opacity-muted yourself to keep it alive: 'muted' is a de-emphasis level and disabled is a state, and sharing one number between them is what put this token on the DELETE-LIST in the first place.

ds-list-item's DOM changed: `[leading]` and `[trailing]` are now siblings of `.activator` rather than children of it, so a row can hold a checkbox or a kebab alongside a row-level action. NO INPUT OR OUTPUT CHANGED -- title, subtitle, clickable, selected, disabled and activated all behave as before, and a plain row looks identical. WHAT MOVED: the row's `display: flex`, its `--ds-list-item-pad-*` padding, its `--ds-list-item-gap`, the hover tint and the selected tint all sit on the HOST now; `.activator` is just the text button and has no padding of its own. ACTION: a `::ng-deep .activator` override that set padding, gap, background or hover now applies to the text only -- move it to `ds-list-item` itself. Also fixed alongside: `selected` set `aria-current` on the inner button, so it was inert whenever `clickable` was false; it is on the host now, which means a non-clickable row marked selected is finally announced as current.

The DEFAULT disabled label colour changed for the two variants that have no container. Was the shared `oklch(from <accent> 70% 0.035 h)`; is now `color-mix(in srgb, <label> 40%, var(--surface-default))` -- the lightness now moves toward the surface instead of being pinned at 70%. WHY: pinned at 70% the disabled label was two points of OKLCH lightness from the enabled one in the DARK theme (--primary-strong is L 67.9% there), a 1.11:1 gap, so a disabled ghost was indistinguishable from an active one. A fixed lightness cannot serve both themes -- in light disabled is lighter than the accent, in dark the accent is already light so disabled must go darker; only the surface knows that direction. Measured after: light 2.54 -> 3.41:1, dark 1.11 -> 2.91:1. NO ACTION NEEDED unless you relied on the exact old colour: `--ds-button-label-color-disabled` is the same hook and still wins, so an app that already sets it sees no change. If you matched the old #949EB5 by hand anywhere (a mock, a screenshot test, a hand-written CSS twin of the disabled state), for the default primary it is now #A5B4F8 in light and #3D4979 in dark. Note the label stays tinted rather than going grey -- chroma rises with the mix (0.036 -> 0.099 in light) -- which was chosen deliberately. `variant="solid"` and `variant="tonal"` are NOT affected and keep the shared recipe; `variant="outline"` is not affected either, for now.

informational: ds-table's row-action kebab and column-picker trigger now read --ds-table-icon-btn-color, --ds-table-icon-btn-color-hover and --ds-table-icon-btn-focus-color, each defaulting to the value that was previously hardcoded (--icon-default, --icon-strong, --accent). Purely additive. ACTION only if you recoloured your own row trigger and are now adopting rowActions: set these three instead of repainting --icon-default globally.

ds-modal and ds-modal-card take per-side padding: --ds-modal-header-pad-top/-pad-bottom, --ds-modal-body-pad-top/-pad-bottom and --ds-modal-actions-pad-top/-pad-bottom. Each defaults to its region's existing --ds-modal-<region>-pad-y, which still works and still sets both edges, so this is purely additive and nothing moves unless you set one. ACTION only if you have been reaching past the API to pad a region asymmetrically - a rule on .modal > .header / > .body / > .actions, most likely carrying !important because the component's own padding outranks a descendant selector: that rule can now be a token on the host instead.
